title: The rwb-case slice of RWB-E2-021 owns no legacy acceptance criterion
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 7; WP B2-P3-007 story line
description: The split gives legacy AC1 to AC12 of RWB-E2-021 to RWB-P6-E2021-APP (rwb-comms) and leaves the rwb-case slice with an empty acs list, so its criteria are written new under D-RCV-60 and test only the case-side deliverables: the hold flag, the timeline facts and the NOTICE_UNSERVED task.
evidence: WP B2-P3-007 story line: "acs": [] and "secondary": true; legacy section 7 holds AC1 to AC12 for the conduct check, the WIN file and the notice state.
proposed: Keep the legacy criteria with RWB-P6-E2021-APP and accept the nine new case-side criteria of this story.

title: The task due date and the task code of an unserved letter are not stated
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 4 and 15; FSD P3 section A2.11
description: The legacy story says the case goes to its owner's queue with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED and that the owner sees MSG-P6-008, and the FSD starts service levels from the timer table, but no source read for this WP gives the task code, the owner role or the due date of that task.
evidence: Legacy section 4 step 7 and section 15 row Unserved; legacy section 13 names no task. FSD P3 A2.11 says service levels and stage timers come from the timer table held as data.
proposed: Hold the task code NOTICE_UNSERVED, the case owner role and the due date from the SERVICE_LEVEL reference row; load the row before the wave starts.

title: No feature flag is named for the rwb-case slice
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 13; FSD P3 A2.26
description: The only flag the legacy story names is rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop, which belongs to rwb-comms. No key is stated for the case-side flag that would turn the hold switch, the ledger facts and the task off in an environment.
evidence: Legacy section 13: "Feature flag: rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop"; no rwb-case flag appears in the FSD P3 feature list.
proposed: Enable the slice with the platform flag mechanism and the P6 dispatch-loop flag, and allocate a key in the parameter catalog at the first build.

title: The operation names and paths of the ledger and decision-record contracts are not in the source set
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12; context pack P3
description: The legacy story calls InteractionLedgerApi.record and DecisionLogApi.write as in-process interfaces. The split makes them REST contracts of rwb-source-data and rwb-decision, and neither operation name nor path appears in the legacy story, the FSD P3, the TSD P3 or the P3 context pack.
evidence: Legacy section 12 rows InteractionLedgerApi.record and DecisionLogApi.write; context pack P3 lists only the operations rwb-case provides.
proposed: Take the paths from the published rwb-source-data and rwb-decision contracts and their fakes; write the REST base per R4 (/api/recovery/source-data/v1, /api/recovery/decision/v1).

title: The interaction ledger is listed in the P3 data model but owned by rwb-source-data
source: TSD P3 T3.1; Ownership Map and DP-18 default ruling
description: TSD P3 T3.1 lists interaction as an object of the P3 module, while the ownership rows of the context pack do not include it and DP-18 with the R-PREC default ruling gives the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data. Source precedence puts the Arch v5 catalogue above the TSD, so the ledger is not owned by rwb-case.
evidence: TSD P3 T3.1 row "interaction (EXTEND ACE activity log)"; context pack P3 ownership tables (15 tables, no interaction); Template and Rules DP-18 row.
proposed: Keep the ledger in rwb-source-data; rwb-case reads and writes it only through that contract and holds no interaction table, view or foreign key.

title: The legal hold reason list is not stated
source: Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 5 and 10; FSD P3 A2.5
description: The legacy story reads legal_hold and cites R-UNI-20 and R-UNI-21, and its authority table says no approval level applies, but no source gives the hold reason list, its codes or the field that carries them.
evidence: Legacy section 5 row X5 and section 10 closing line; FSD P3 A2.5 exclusion lists, TSD P3 T3.2 lists of values (no hold-reason list).
proposed: Hold the reason list as a reference table of rwb-case loaded by RW-COE; the reason is stored as given until the list is approved.
